business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

France-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (DTA, 1968/2019 protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-2-2, L.561-45 to L.561-57 and R.561-20-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by LOI n°2016-1691 (Sapin II), LOI n°2020-1722, and Decree No. 2018-1044; Articles R.123-166 and R.123-223 of the French Commercial Code; EU AMLD4/AMLD5 Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of parent entity Certificate of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar of origin, countersigned by local notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association (Statuts)
Certificate of Good Standing or Compliance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies in the jurisdiction of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO register extract for every shareholder holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent domestic UBO registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if origin is not a Hague Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent bank reference letter evidencing funding source for bunker inventories or vessel/fuel contracts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or bank-certified signature + apostille if requested

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and commercial counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, TRACFIN typology indicators, French Treasury list (FCPG), and the French Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) register. Enhanced due diligence is required where any beneficial owner is a PEP, where payment originates from a sanction-sensitive jurisdiction, or where the bunkering counterparty history is shorter than three years. Screening must be repeated no later than 48 hours before incorporation and 48 hours before each bunkering transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for company formation filings; RCS consultation via Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be in any language but, if written in a non-Latin script, a Latin-character transliteration is mandatory for RCS indexing and for AML matching. The statutory bylaws (statuts) are binding in the French version; where a foreign language version exists, the French text prevails for all domestic purposes. Loi Toubon requires official contract documentation, invoices, and product safety information to be issued in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested corporate name is rejected by the INPI Guichet Unique or the competent commercial registry, the applicant may first file a formal reconsideration request through the portal with a clear legal basis. If the rejection is confirmed, an administrative appeal must be lodged before the Tribunal de Commerce or Tribunal Judiciaire having jurisdiction within two months of the rejection notice. The appeal brief must annex the certificate of negativity, the counsel's submission, and documentary proof of the clearing of any objection raised by the registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a pure virtual address. A SAS must have a physical registered office in France, which may be provided by an authorized domiciliation company (agréée) maintaining a physical reception facility, mail-holding, and archival records in compliance with Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. A mailbox-only virtual address will trigger regulatory rejection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing registration and corporate formalities; Article L.561-46 of the Monetary and Financial Code governing beneficial-owner filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Single Business Formalities Portal for filing, with registration in the Registre National des Entreprises and the competent local Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés maintained by the commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of creation and registration of a commercial company through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, supported by the signed SAS articles of association and beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed and may require a commissaire aux apports report, subject to statutory exemptions. No general escrow account is required, although a blocked capital-deposit account is normally used until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the Company has been duly incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée and approves the subscription and payment of the shares specified in the articles of association. The Board confirms the Company’s registered office at the address stated in the incorporation file and authorizes filing with the Guichet Unique and the competent commercial court registry. The Board appoints [name] as President and, if applicable, [name] as Directeur Général, each accepting the relevant office and authority. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, obtain tax and customs registrations, and execute all documents required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate name, purpose, address, and shareholder structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises and the competent local commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve or verify the proposed corporate name, confirm a valid French registered office, define the bunkering and marine-lubricant activity precisely, identify shareholders and officers, and determine whether regulated port, environmental, customs, or petroleum activities will be conducted directly by the SAS.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and business purpose
Shareholder identification documents and ownership percentages
Officer identification documents and signed acceptance of office
Corporate authorization and certified registry extract for corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the name, purpose, address, or identification data before submission; obtain written landlord or domiciliation-provider confirmation where the registry questions the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SAS constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notarial or legal-document execution process; filing through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association covering share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance, President powers, approval rights, financial year, and dissolution rules. Execute the articles electronically or in wet ink. Notarization is generally not required for cash contributions, but notarized instruments are required where real estate is contributed or another transaction is subject to mandatory notarization.
required_dossiers: Commissaire aux apports report or waiver, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective clauses, obtain missing signatures, commission an independent contribution report where required, and re-execute the affected documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and obtain the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or authorized deposit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash capital, provide the executed articles and shareholder identification documents, and obtain the certificate of deposit. The certificate must identify the company under formation, deposited amount, and subscribers. Release of funds normally follows evidence of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC or source-of-funds queries, replace incomplete identification documents, and obtain a written refusal if the institution will not accept the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation formalities and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic declaration of creation, upload the articles, capital-deposit certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, publication notice, and beneficial-owner information, then pay the applicable registration charges. Select the commercial activity and include the relevant marine-fuel, lubricant, logistics, and port-service descriptions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the INPI or registry deficiency notice within the stated deadline, upload corrected documents, pay any supplementary fee, and resubmit through the portal if the filing is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration and complete post-incorporation registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI RNE, tax administration, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, verify the registered activity and NAF classification, release the capital, activate the permanent bank account, and complete VAT, corporate-tax, employer, customs, and intra-EU registrations as applicable. Establish accounting, invoicing, sanctions-screening, AML, and fuel-traceability controls.
required_dossiers: Customs EORI application, if importing or exporting
Employment registrations, if personnel are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of inaccurate registry data, contact the tax service for VAT or tax-account activation, and submit an EORI or URSSAF correction request where the registration is incomplete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve governance records and operational delegations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company governance bodies; relevant port, customs, environmental, and occupational authorities for delegated operational roles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or shareholder resolutions required by the articles, confirm officer appointments, establish signing authorities, approve bank mandates, appoint auditors where legally required, and document delegations for HSSE, bunkering operations, dangerous-goods compliance, customs, and environmental reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt ratifying resolutions, correct minutes, replace unauthorized signatories, and file any mandatory changes with the registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The relevant prefecture for installations classified for environmental protection (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l’Environnement, or ICPE), supported by the applicable DREAL; the competent port authority or port concessionaire for port access, terminal operations, bunkering permissions, ship-to-ship activity, and occupation of port property; and the Directorate-General for Customs and Indirect Taxes for customs and excise requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE environmental authorization or registration, as applicable to the storage, handling, transfer, or distribution installation, together with a port operating authorization, terminal agreement, or port concession and any required authorization for handling petroleum products or dangerous goods. France has no single nationwide generic manufacturing license for ship bunkering.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry for Ecological Transition, acting through the competent prefecture and DREAL, with the competent regional environmental authority (Mission Régionale d’Autorité environnementale, or MRAe) or the Conseil général de l’environnement et du développement durable where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site-specific: full environmental authorization and environmental assessment may be required for qualifying storage, fuel-transfer, port, or hazardous-material installations; registration or declaration may apply to lower-threshold ICPE activities. A case-by-case screening determination is required before construction or operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE ministerial order, prefectural authorization, Water Act requirements, port rules, and EU environmental standards. Maintain containment and spill-prevention systems, manage hazardous waste through authorized channels, control VOC and vapor emissions where applicable, and meet permit-specific wastewater discharge limits. Marine operations must also comply with MARPOL, including Annex I oil-pollution controls, bunkering procedures, spill-response equipment, recordkeeping, and applicable fuel-sulfur limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire-prevention and emergency-response approval from the competent fire and rescue service and prefectural or port authority where required; complete structural, loading, containment, electrical, hazardous-area, and pressure-equipment inspections; implement the French Labour Code risk-assessment and occupational-safety requirements; appoint competent dangerous-goods and HSSE personnel; maintain emergency plans, employee training, personal protective equipment, contractor controls, and documented bunkering procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — national tax authority; online portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional space: espace-pro.impots.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in France must register with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) via the SIRENE registry or through the dedicated online procedure on impots.gouv.fr. The entity obtains a SIRET number (unique establishment identifier) and a VAT identification number (TVA intracommunautaire) for EU-wide transactions. A fiscal representative must be appointed if the entity carries out taxable operations in France without being established in the EU.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SAS is by default subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS). Under limited conditions, a new SAS may elect for income tax application (régime fiscal des sociétés de personnes) for 5 years, but this election is unavailable for most commercial activities and must be disregarded for active marine bunkering. No check-the-box election exists in France; hybrid mismatch elections follow EU ATAD implementation, mainly internal safe-harbour provisions requiring filing with the DGFiP in annual returns.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for supplies of goods or services performed in France by foreign entities; any taxable person making taxable supplies in France must register from the first euro. For E-commerce/non-established distance sellers, the EU-wide distance sales threshold applies (EUR 10,000 across all EU member states). Domestic micro-businesses may benefit from the EUR 91,900 (goods) / EUR 36,800 (services) exemption thresholds under Article 293 B CGI, but foreign suppliers cannot rely on these exemptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for B2B domestic transactions is being phased in from 1 September 2026 (large enterprises) and 1 September 2027 (SMEs), using structured electronic formats (E-invoicing via PEPPOL/SEML/FACTUR-X) and mandatory e-reporting E-reporting is transmitted in real time through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), requiring API or certified partner connection. Invoices must fulfil authentication requirements, and no perpetual digital fiscal stamping is applied, but real-time clearance controls increasingly apply via the PPF.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the European Union may be zero-rated for French VAT if the exporter proves dispatch/transport outside the EU under Article 262-1 CGI. For marine bunkering and lubricant replenishment, supplies of fuel and lubricants to vessels engaged in international navigation are zero-rated or exempt under Articles 262-II-1° and 278-0 bis A CGI, provided the vessel falls under the definition of international transport (or maritime shipping for more than 20 days or commercial voyages). The service must be physically supplied at the vessel's location; supply to EU flagged vessels on intra-EU routes is generally taxable. Supporting evidence must demonstrate that the vessel fulfills the qualification of 'international traffic' and the fuel was loaded onboard.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane, DELTA / EXA electronic documentation with the France Customs Single Window (GUN) certificate)
Bill of Lading (or, where applicable, sea waybill / mate's receipt)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Payment Confirmation showing the export proceeds received on a French or foreign bank account
Bunker Delivery Receipt / Delivery Note signed by the ship's master or authorized vessel agent
Contract or sale agreement for marine fuel/bunkers identifying vessel name, IMO number, port of supply, and quantity
Proof of vessel's international navigation status (e.g., ship registry certificate, voyage itinerary)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to strict documentary proof. In case of fraud or unjustified zero-rating, the French tax authorities may issue an assessment for unpaid VAT plus late payment interest (0.2% per month), late filing penalties (5% to 40% of the tax), a 40% tax delinquency penalty for intentional misstatements, and up to a 80% penalty in case of abusive fraud or opposition to tax inspection. Criminal prosecution for customs or VAT fraud may result in imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to EUR 375,000 as well as potential revocation of the exporter's VAT registration and extended audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with prudential supervision of credit institutions delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments administration co-ordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Code monétaire et financier, notably Articles L151-2 to L151-4, L561-1 et seq., and the règlement général de l'ACPR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a full euro-area convertibility regime and accepts IMF Article VIII obligations; capital movements and payments are liberalised within the EU under TFEU Articles 63-65 and vis-à-vis third countries, subject only to (i) EU/UN financial sanctions and asset-freezing measures, (ii) prior authorisation under the French foreign-direct-investment screening mechanism for strategic sectors covering energy-supply security and dual-use activities, which may require a clearance opinion if a non-resident parent acquires control of a port fuel logistics SAS, and (iii) prudential statistical reporting thresholds. Current-account transactions, including bunker sales abroad, freight settlements, agency commissions and marine lubricant purchases, are freely executable without FX licence or advance declaration. Profit remittance is unrestricted via ordinary dividend distributions, subject to French withholding tax at the standard non-treaty rate of 25%, reducible to 0% for a qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive corporate shareholder or reduced under double-tax treaties for non-EU shareholders, together with the obligation to file Form 2561 and to substantiate beneficial ownership under anti-money-laundering rules. No exchange-control visa is required to open a capital escrow account in favour of the SAS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No French or EU statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation deadline applies to export or bunkering proceeds; export earnings may be retained indefinitely in USD, EUR or any freely convertible currency. Bunkering of vessels engaged in international navigation is classified as an export of goods under the EU VAT Directive (Articles 146-148) and qualifies for zero-rated VAT and excise exemption under Articles 262 and 162 of the Code général des impôts, with commercial documentation required to evidence the international voyage. The sole regulatory constraint is the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting régime (RONO): payments to or from non-residents equal to or exceeding EUR 15,000 per individual transaction, or cumulative monthly cross-border flows above EUR 150,000, must be captured and reported by the intermediary bank; the SAS must code each wire with the correct purpose description, such as exportation de biens - approvisionnement de navires, apport en capital, dividende or compensation, so that non-existent surrender obligations are not de facto triggered by miscoded remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. French-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Blank and Shine, chartered by the ACPR under the PSD2 framework, can deliver rapid IBAN collection, multi-currency wallets and digital invoicing for a newly formed SAS, and are suitable for transit liquidity and regular operating payments up to prudent commercial caps. However, an EMI is not a substitute for a full credit institution: it cannot issue standby letters of credit or commercial documentary credits, cannot grant overdrafts or revolving credit facilities, and must hold client funds under the e-money safeguarding régime, which prevents the construction of a true capital escrow plus LC treasury hub. Cross-border EEA EMIs holding a valid passport may onboard the SAS remotely, whereas UK-regulated EMIs have lost EU passporting rights after Brexit and cannot lawfully serve the French market without establishing a French branch. For capital escrow, SWIFT MT103 liquidity and Standby-LC issuance, a Tier-1 commercial bank account remains mandatory as the treasury backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, physical presence is required for non-resident directors and for the SAS opening operating accounts in the marine-bunkering sector, which is classified by ACPR as Medium-Risk Enhanced. French AML law permits video-identification under Article R561-5 of the Code monétaire et financier and the 2019 ACPR position, but Tier-1 banks generally condition full corporate onboarding on (i) an in-person or notarially attested meeting at a bank branch or at the registered office with the legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owner, (ii) production of the notarised SAS statuts, (iii) delivery of the current Kbis extract and the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) filed with INPI, and (iv) execution of original mandates and specimen signature cards. Remote onboarding is typically refused where the UBO resides in a sanctioned or non-cooperative jurisdiction. The efficient route is to appoint a resident directeur général or finance manager who attends the interview, supplemented by an apostilled power of attorney for the non-resident founder, plus evidence of source of funds through six-month parent-company bank statements and a funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual or opaque holding-chain UBO with nominal SAS share capital and no identifiable French economic substance (shell-structure red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) filed with INPI; current Kbis extract; notarised statuts; apostilled parent-company registry extract; UBO passport, proof of address and tax residence; group organisational chart evidencing substance; auditor's confirmation of economic activity and physical office presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine bunkering exposure to vessels flying flags of convenience (Panama, Liberia, Marshall Islands, Comoros) or calls to sanctioned ports (Syria, Crimea, restricted Russian Far East ports under current EU packages)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IHS Markit/Equasis vessel registration snapshot showing the IMO number; flag certificate and certificate of registry; ISM and ISPS compliance certificates; P&I Club entry evidence (ITOPF/Shiptowners Mutual); 12-month AIS tracking extract; charter party or bunker delivery note stating the international-voyage purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-like or third-party payments at port terminals in support of bunker deliveries (trade-based money-laundering red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented zero-cash treasury policy; electronic metering and fuel-management system records; BIMCO bunker terms contract; bank-to-bank MT103 remittances matched to invoices by unique reference; independent terminal surveyor (SGS/Cotecna) volume and quality reports; prohibition of cash settlement above EUR 1,000 as mandated by French law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty set includes wholesale bunker traders domiciled in low-enforcement or low-tax jurisdictions, including Malta, Gibraltar, Marshall Islands and certain EEA entities with thin substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive counterparty KYC file: public registry extracts, Orbis/Bureau van Dijk credit reports, UBO declarations, World-Check negative-screening result, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions and OFAC screening certificate dated within 30 days, PEP check, and contractual warranties of lawful origin of fuel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large shareholder loans or capital injections from an intra-group treasury lacking traceable source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of parent-company bank statements; board minutes approving the capital increase or shareholder advance; signed shareholder loan agreement with OECD-compliant arm's-length interest; audited group financial statements; tax-residency certificate of the foreign parent; funds-flow diagram from ultimate source to SAS account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 15,000 per transaction or EUR 150,000 per month without coherent SWIFT purpose coding, triggering RONO reporting failures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardised ISO 20022 payment ecosystem with mapped Banque de France purpose codes; automatic reconciliation through MT940/camt.054 statements; monthly balance-of-payments register maintained by the appointed accountancy function; written purpose-code mapping table covering approvisionnement de navires, apport en capital, dividende and supplier settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of standby letters of credit and guarantees could indicate undisclosed contingent off-balance-sheet risk without clearing approval
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ICC ISP98-compliant SBLC issuance executed exclusively through the licensed credit institution; internal credit-policy memorandum signed by the Président de la SAS; guarantees register; risk-concentration monitoring aligned with the bank's regulatory capital approval and internal delegated authority limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Post-opening change in beneficial ownership, including transfer of shares to a trust or offshore private foundation, triggering ongoing client due-diligence failure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ongoing CDD refresh completed at least annually; account-mandate clause requiring immediate notification of any UBO change; INPI RBE amendment filings; notarised share-transfer deeds; declarations of trust or foundation structure; updated group chart and sanctions re-screening certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended inbound routing for the French SAS: (1) open a dedicated capital-injection escrow sub-account with BNP Paribas or Société Générale, ring-fenced from trading operations; (2) execute the subscription via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's clearing bank with remittance information stating CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - SAS FR_SAS - REGISTRATION NO and the Banque de France purpose code EQUITY - APPORT EN CAPITAL; (3) attach the board minutes approving the reserved capital increase, notary or signature validation, shareholder identification and intra-group VAT status; (4) ensure that any individual wire of EUR 15,000 or more, or cumulative monthly flows above EUR 150,000, is automatically captured by the receiving bank under the RONO balance-of-payments reporting régime; (5) where the foreign parent remits USD, pre-book a same-day EUR/USD spot conversion through the French bank to eliminate FX drag; (6) file the capital-increase amendment with the INPI registry and update the RBE within the statutory one-month window; (7) retain bank confirmation of source of funds and economic purpose to satisfy FATF-aligned French AML obligations, including the prohibition of anonymous accounts. A subordinated shareholder loan (compte courant d'associé) can complement equity capital using the same SWIFT routing with purpose code SHAREHOLDER LOAN - COMPTE COURANT ASSOCIE, supported by a written loan agreement bearing an arm's-length interest rate to prevent tax recharacterisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for bunkering disbursements are structured across four layers: Layer 1, SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated EU/EEA suppliers, covering port service calls, lubricant replenishment from Rotterdam/Antwerp terminals and barge logistics; Layer 2, SWIFT MT103 corporate wires for USD-restated FOB cargo-priced fuel purchases, executed through the direct correspondent USD nostro concentration of BNP Paribas or Société Générale, with mandatory OFAC and EU sanctions filtering on every wire; Layer 3, commercial documentary letters of credit under ICC UCP 600 and eUCP 2.0 for term-based refinery and large-flexi purchases, issued by the Tier-1 French bank on a sight or 15/30/60-day tenor basis with presentation of bunker delivery notes, quantity certificates and commercial invoices; Layer 4, Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98 issued by the Tier-1 bank as security for delivery performance or post-fuelling payment obligations to ship operators and suppliers. Supplementary mechanisms include assignment of receivables (cession Dailly) under French law for bunker-receivables financing, daily MT940/camt.053 cash-position reports, a payment factory with automated sanctions screening, and an integrated bank fuel-card for high-frequency small port dispatches. Cash disbursements are prohibited above EUR 1,000 under French law, and no treasury disbursement may be executed without a matched invoice, vessel IMO reference and port-call record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable currency forwards up to 24 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, compliant with French financial-markets regulation and the AMF regime, used to hedge USD-indexed bunker sales and USD/Brent arbitration pricing.
EUR/USD FX swaps and rolling swaps to manage tenor and value-date mismatches between USD receipt dates and EUR liability dates, particularly for weekly port-billing cycles.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to hedge long-dated financing where bunker-supply debt is USD-denominated and the SAS revenue base is EUR, subject to board-approved hedge documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies, including USD/CNH offshore and USD/KRW, used exclusively to hedge supplier invoices denominated in non-convertible Asian currencies, booked under the bank's EMIR-compliant clearing desk.

Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (risk reversals) to cap adverse USD appreciation while retaining favourable movement, executed only within a board-approved treasury policy that preserves hedge-accounting eligibility under IFRS 9.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: French corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 May of the following year for calendar-year taxpayer; within 5 months of fiscal year-end if a non-calendar close is adopted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic increase; if unfiled after formal notice, 40% increase and default interest of 0.4% per month; criminal fine and director disqualification possible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of close of fiscal year, e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order to file within 1 month plus astreinte (penalty) up to €1,500 per day; administrative dissolution and RCS strike-off for persistent failure; director disqualification exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with each annual accounts deposit; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Legal entity fine up to €20,000 for omission or inaccurate declaration; personal fine and up to 2 years imprisonment in case of deliberate false statement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local company contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises - CFE) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Départementale des Finances Publiques (local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration filed in May each year; payment due by 15 December of the same tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment increases tax by 10% plus monthly interest of 0.20%; enforced recovery and seizure of assets for habitual non-payment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (Commissaire aux comptes) is compulsory for any SAS exceeding two of three thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet > €4 million, net turnover (excl. VAT) > €8 million, and average French headcount > 50 employees; group-audit appointment may also be required if the SAS is a consolidating parent or holds a controlled subsidiary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG - Plan Comptable Général / ANC Regulation 2014-03) for individual statutory statements; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of listed or EU-listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owners (BO) must be confirmed with the RCS each year on the annual accounts filing; any share transfer leading to a BO change requires an amended UBO declaration within 30 days; the company must also maintain an internal ownership register (registre des mouvements de titres) and minute records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute Book (Registre des assemblées et procès-verbaux)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying small or medium-sized company may apply the 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and fully paid-up share capital held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate described above is the principal generally available reduced corporate rate. Other relief may apply only if the SAS independently meets the conditions of a specific regime, such as qualifying research and development credits or a geographically targeted incentive. No general tax holiday applies to marine bunkering. Bunkering operations may separately trigger VAT, excise-duty, customs, and environmental obligations; those do not reduce the IS rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual deduction ceiling of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A one-year carryback is generally available, capped at EUR 1 million, subject to election and statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with the applicable detailed schedules—generally Forms 2050 to 2059 for the normal regime or Forms 2033-A to 2033-G for the simplified regime—filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal, impots.gouv.fr, using the EDI-TDFC transmission route or the applicable online filing service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; quarterly IS instalments may be required during the financial year. Companies below the statutory instalment exemption threshold may be exempt from instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the electronic filing deadline is generally the second working day after 1 May, subject to the tax administration's published calendar. The IS balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 15 May. Quarterly instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN, registered address, tax office, financial-year dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. Use the SAS's French SIREN and registered details; identify foreign shareholders and related parties in the relevant schedules where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss after reconciling the accounting result to French tax rules and completing the applicable tax schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include profits attributable to the French SAS. A non-resident shareholder should not report the SAS's operating profit as its own French corporate income unless a separate taxable presence or other French-source income rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the balance sheet, income statement, tax adjustments, provisions, fixed assets, depreciation, and other information required by the company's tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French accounting and tax rules to the French entity's records. Disclose cross-border related-party transactions in the applicable transfer-pricing reporting and documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate IS at the applicable rate, claim eligible credits or reductions, and account for instalments and withholding credits where legally available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally attributable to the SAS and supported by records. Treaty relief for a shareholder's dividend withholding is claimed through the relevant withholding procedure, not as a reduction of the SAS's operating taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete required disclosures, including distributions and other information requested by the form and applicable schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report distributions to non-residents and ensure withholding, beneficial-owner, and treaty-relief records are maintained. Submit any separately required transfer-pricing return, including Form 2257-SD where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge on tax due where no formal notice has been served, 40% after a formal notice remains unremedied, and 80% in cases such as discovery of an undeclared activity or certain abuses. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge. Default interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and exceptions. Inaccurate or incomplete returns may attract additional penalties based on the nature and seriousness of the breach.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic withholding rate on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty reduction. A 12.8% domestic rate generally applies to individual recipients, subject to applicable rules. Qualifying EU/EEA parent companies may obtain an exemption under the French parent-subsidiary regime, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the beneficial owner should provide the French payer with the applicable French tax-residence certificate (TRC) and treaty claim documentation, commonly the relevant Form 5000 and, for dividends, Form 5001, or the applicable electronic or refund procedure. The payer applies a reduced rate or exemption only when statutory documentation and eligibility conditions are met; otherwise, domestic withholding generally applies and the recipient may seek a refund. Confirm the relevant bilateral treaty, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions, beneficial ownership, and any required holding period. A TRC alone does not establish entitlement to treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding, subject to a lower treaty rate, an applicable EU directive exemption, and domestic exceptions. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding, but a 75% rate may apply to payments to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions, subject to statutory conditions and exceptions. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment type; verify the applicable treaty and anti-abuse requirements before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) generally applies where the French entity's annual turnover, gross assets, or specified group relationship thresholds reach EUR 400 million, including applicable thresholds for a controlling or controlled group entity. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at a EUR 50 million threshold, subject to statutory group and ownership tests. Thresholds and scope should be tested against the current French rules and the relevant fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not impose a general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore regimes. French rules nevertheless require genuine commercial rationale and may deny benefits or adjust results under transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, the abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, and other anti-avoidance provisions. The SAS should maintain evidence of decision-making, personnel, assets, risk control, contracts, and operational capacity consistent with its stated bunkering functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, falsifying invoices or books, or knowingly filing materially false returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, and surcharges may apply. Intentional fraud may be referred for criminal prosecution; serious tax fraud can result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with higher penalties possible in aggravated cases under the French Tax Code and Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability where they participated in, directed, or knowingly facilitated the offence. A court may impose fines and imprisonment; tax debts may be imposed personally in defined cases of fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated non-compliance. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing misstatement and undocumented related-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing fuel, lubricant, financing, services, or intangibles with related parties on non-arm's-length terms; failing to produce required documentation; or omitting required disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable profit may be adjusted, with interest and applicable surcharges. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions concerned, subject to statutory conditions and caps; separate penalties may apply to incomplete or inaccurate disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for intentional participation in fraud or for specified serious breaches, but ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically pierce the corporate veil. Maintain contemporaneous benchmarking, intercompany agreements, and evidence supporting functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without observing corporate-law distribution rules, applying treaty relief without eligibility or adequate proof, or failing to withhold and remit tax when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and surcharges. Improper distributions may be recoverable under French company law and may expose responsible persons to civil or criminal consequences depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability where statutory conditions for fraudulent conduct, misappropriation, or serious tax non-compliance are met. Treaty relief should be supported by current residence and beneficial-ownership evidence and reviewed before payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a conduit without genuine functions or decision-making, misrepresenting beneficial ownership, or claiming treaty or tax benefits through an arrangement lacking commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authorities may deny treaty or tax benefits, recharacterize transactions, assess tax and interest, and apply abuse-of-law penalties. Criminal sanctions may apply if the arrangement involves fraud, forged records, or concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability depends on the director's conduct and the applicable civil or criminal provisions; limited liability is not a defense to a director's own fraud or criminal acts. A travel ban is not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions, and illicit bunkering proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly handling proceeds of crime, disguising vessel ownership or cargo origin, evading applicable sanctions, or failing to meet applicable anti-money-laundering and customer due-diligence duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Depending on the offence, sanctions may include criminal fines, imprisonment, asset seizure or confiscation, administrative measures, and restrictions on business activity. Penalties depend on the specific AML, sanctions, customs, and criminal-law provisions breached.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other responsible persons may be prosecuted for their own participation, instruction, or knowing facilitation. Corporate status does not shield personal criminal liability; imprisonment and asset confiscation may apply where authorized by law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting fuel supply, storage, transport, customs, or regulated-port operations without required authorizations, or breaching applicable safety, environmental, excise, or customs controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include administrative fines, suspension or withdrawal of authorizations, tax and excise reassessments, seizure of goods, and criminal sanctions where the relevant breach is an offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for personal participation or for specific statutory management offences. Confirm permits, port and customs procedures, excise treatment, and environmental requirements for each operating location and product.
